Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Chigils appear to have formed the nucleus of the _____ army

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The date of its foundation and the name of its first khan is uncertain, but according to one reconstruction, the first Karakhanid ruler was Bilge Kul Qadir Khan.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The names of animals were a regular element in the Turkic titles of the _____: thus Aslan (lion), Bughra (camel), Toghan (falcon), Böri (wolf), and Toghrul or Toghrïl (a bird of prey)

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Later they adopted the Arab titles sultan and sultān al-salātīn ("Sultan of Sultans").

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: According to the Ottoman historian called Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Khanate conquered _____ in Central Asia and ruled it independently between 999 and 1089

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Musa (title: Kara Khan or Arslan Khan) resumed the campaign against the Samanids, and by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Samanid domains were divided between the Ghaznavids, who gained Khorasan and Afghanistan, and the Karakhanids, who received Transoxiana.
